# Scene input trace after checkpoint 534

At pinned revision ff9c1d7d0ea168b7e14eedc5e44879ee7b84fb04, the fresh
server generation route passes generated.ground to spawn_scene. The
GeneratedTacticalScene declaration requires SceneGround, and spawn_scene
queues it with SceneId before inserting SceneTerrain. Replication registers
SceneId, SceneTerrain, and SceneGround individually.

Evidence locators: tactical-core/src/scene_input/generated.rs lines 7–22,
tactical-server/src/main.rs lines 702–711, tactical-server/src/terrain_collision.rs
lines 20–39, and tactical-netcode/src/replication.rs lines 59–61.

The dump route deserializes and writes a reflected world separately. Its
terrain observer can attach replication and collision from SceneTerrain
without checking SceneGround in that observer. Trace restoration validation
and the supported dump fixtures before deciding ground completeness there.
Also check delivery and observer ordering before assigning client-side
completeness. Register and reread these pinned bodies before formal adoption.

The dump writer explicitly allows SceneId and SceneTerrain but omits
SceneGround and SceneEnvironment. The terrain-added observer reconstructs
collision and replication using terrain with optional recipe/patch, without
inserting either omitted component. The loader applies the reflected scene
and flushes observers. This establishes an apparent dump round-trip gap in
scene inputs. Check for other restoration hooks and client defaults before
classifying its effect on readiness, and formally register these sources
before awarding audit credit. No runtime reproduction has been performed.
Evidence locators at ff9c1d7: tactical-server/src/debug_dump.rs lines 30–54,
terrain_collision.rs lines 41–72, and main.rs lines 311–362.

A bounded search of tactical-server sources finds SceneGround and
SceneEnvironment references only in spawn_scene's inputs. Client environment
selection activates on adding SceneEnvironment and selects among existing
environment-bearing entities (presentation/environment.rs lines 16–48).
This supports a restore gap for dumps produced by the current allowlist, though
full client-side insertion paths and runtime behavior remain unverified. Search
output for environment was truncated, so it is a locator, not exhaustive proof.

Debug startup sets generate_terrain to false when a world dump is supplied
(main.rs 643–665), so the fresh spawn path does not supply missing scene
components in that mode. SceneReadiness counts every SceneTerrain and requires
separate ground-layer markers in its counts. The exact loading gate and the
client insertion paths still need qualification before claiming a hang.

LoadingSources sets GroundCover progress to the number of scatter and grass
markers over twice the number of terrain scenes (loading_screen/sources.rs
13–14, 38–40, 73–81). Terrain's environment and ground observers insert
PendingTerrainPresentation when those components arrive (terrain.rs 710–727).
A scene lacking both may therefore be counted as terrain-presented merely
because the pending marker is absent, while ground cover remains incomplete
if no other system supplies its required inputs. Confirm insertion coverage
and the screen completion policy before asserting an observed hang.

LoadingRun reports Stalled at the first unfinished stage after 90 seconds of
unchanged progress in game time (progress.rs 6–10, 113–117, 161–179). Thus a
persistent missing ground-cover marker would lead to a stall verdict rather
than an indefinite wait. The earlier Vista stage may be the reported stage.
This remains a source-based conditional, not a runtime reproduction.

The planned ranges were reread without output truncation on this continuation.
They confirm the allowlist, startup branch, terrain observer, ground-layer
count and 90-second stall rule. The registered terrain observer range ends
inside its closure, so its final lines must be registered and read before
claiming the full observer body. These observations have not been adopted
into the verified audit queue or credited as completed lens cells.

The complete terrain observer body was reread through line 75. It adds
Replicated, removes the prepared patch, and creates collider children, with
no ground or environment insertion. This narrows the restore investigation
but does not establish that no other system supplies the missing components.

Checkpoint 534 verification passed on this continuation. Entry 1411 already
owns the scene-population question and explicitly calls for admitted ground,
replication, spawn and reset lifecycle evidence. The dump trace is a candidate
qualification for that entry. Its receipt, source hashes and precise repair
relationship still need to be assembled before altering the queue.

Correction to the earlier conditional about terrain being counted as presented:
SceneId addition also inserts PendingTerrainPresentation (terrain.rs 66–73).
The dump allowlist includes SceneId, so a normal restored scene with that
component should create pending work when the client observes it. Observer and
replication ordering still require qualification. The previous suggestion that
missing ground and environment alone leave the marker absent was incomplete.

PresentationPlugin registers the SceneId, environment and ground observers
(presentation/mod.rs 317–320). Netcode registers SceneId, SceneTerrain,
SceneGround and SceneEnvironment as separate replicated components
(replication.rs 59–62). This establishes registration, but does not establish
when the client's observer runs relative to component application. These are
exploratory locators, with no audit credit or runtime reproduction.

The existing world_dump_round_trips_through_load test in main.rs 520–620
constructs a player and sword and asserts their restored relationship. Its
fixture contains no terrain, ground or environment, so it does not establish
the scene-input round trip. This is a test-scope observation, not a test run.

SceneGround derives Reflect and Serde, while SceneEnvironment derives Serde
but not Reflect at its declaration (scene/ground.rs 18–28 and
scene_input/environment.rs 5–25). Adding both directly to a reflected dump
allowlist therefore needs further reflection/serialization design analysis.
These are exploratory source observations, not a tested repair.

TacticalSceneInput::environment_snapshot derives environment from the current
input and a supplied digest (scene_input.rs 166–200). Reconstructing from the
current input would require proving it matches the input used by the dumped
scene. The dump currently does not retain SceneEnvironment's digest, so this
source alone does not establish that equality. No repair choice is selected.

Startup loads scene input from its own argument even in standalone dump mode
(main.rs 119–137). The inspected startup section does not compare it with the
dump. The StartupInputs implementation remains to be read before drawing a
broader conclusion. Two read-only Git commands are still running and must be
polled before retrying them (sessions 58948 and 86049).

Both pending source queries completed successfully. StartupInputs::load reads
an explicitly supplied scene path or the default scene path and validates that
input (startup.rs 51–73). Its arguments do not include the dump path, and this
function does not compare scene input with dump provenance. This supports
retaining provenance as a repair obligation, subject to the rest of startup.

The dump loader is scheduled after server startup on entering Running
(main.rs 262–266). Its complete previously inspected body (311–362) reads,
deserializes and writes the scene, with no input-digest comparison. Combined
with StartupInputs::load, this establishes that these specific startup and
load functions do not bind the supplied input to dump provenance. Other
systems and runtime behavior remain outside this observation.

The independently loaded input builds the vista bundle, including its digest,
properties and extents (scene_setup.rs 18–36), and startup always creates world
bounds from that input (main.rs 657–663, 712). If a dump and supplied input
differ, those derived values can describe a different scene from the restored
terrain. This is a conditional source inference, not a reproduced mismatch.

The furniture restore test constructs its original and restored vista bundles
from the same input and checks restored furniture groups, distant furniture and
collision. It does not exercise a mismatched input or terrain/environment
round trip (debug_dump_world_tests/furniture_restore.rs). This qualifies the
existing test coverage without asserting a runtime failure.

Ground generation depends on prepared environment, terrain, obstacles,
buildings, streets and yards (generation/geographic.rs 20–63). Substituting a
default ground during restore would discard semantic data. A reconstruction
strategy must preserve the original input and generation contract or carry the
generated ground itself. This is a scoped source inference, not a chosen repair.

The supported-terrain phase carries geographic ground unchanged while applying
property support to terrain. generate_unfurnished then passes that ground to
furniture generation and returns it in GeneratedTacticalScene
(generation/supported.rs 22–54 and generation.rs 21–54). This narrows the
source lineage for preservation, without proving deterministic regeneration
across versions or a complete snapshot strategy.

Entry 1411 remains open and has an unresolved canonical owner. Its existing
scene-readiness view connects this investigation, but the entry's broader
native and retained-state questions remain separate. The restore trace alone
cannot close it or establish an alias. A scoped source view should preserve
those obligations and distinguish the conditional dump defect from a runtime
witness.

Related entries 1328, 3799 and 3800 cover ground-scatter wiring and distinct
native asset admission/publication questions. The dump input omission supplies
context for a missing query population, but does not settle those asset lifetime
or failure-disposition questions. Preserve their separate ownership and evidence
requirements when adopting the restore view.

PendingScenes requires SceneId, SceneTerrain and SceneEnvironment, with ground
optional (terrain/volumetric.rs 4–17). A restored scene carrying SceneId and
terrain but missing environment cannot match this terrain producer query.
Given normal client observation of SceneId, pending terrain remains until the
missing environment arrives or another lifecycle action changes the entity.
Replication timing and actual dump execution remain unverified.

A scoped exact-name search across tactical-server source finds SceneEnvironment
only as the spawn_scene parameter. main.rs constructs it via
input.environment_snapshot and passes it to spawn_scene. This supports its
initial-snapshot lineage, but cannot rule out generic or external component
mutation. The component is declared immutable in its defining source.

Next current-delta scope selected: procedural-textures/src/runtime.rs, path 0
in delta 2, with all 13 lens cells open. The pinned diff adds installed_count,
which counts requested recipe IDs present in installed residency. Existing
checkpoint 534 registered both source revisions. Assess duplicate recipe IDs,
consumer population, reset lifecycle and each lens independently before any
cell closure. Diff inspection is a locator and grants no source credit.

Residency retains requested container handles and an installed ID set. The new
count filters the caller's iterator, so duplicate input IDs count repeatedly.
The loading caller passes catalogue IDs and uses catalogue length as its total.
A catalogue uniqueness test exists, but has not been run or inspected in full.
Installation inserts IDs after installing maps. Asset eviction, reload and
native acknowledgement remain separate obligations. Source read is scoped and
no lens cell has been closed.

The current catalogue lists 24 distinct recipe identifiers and its test
asserts ID uniqueness (catalogue.rs 138–177). The residency test requests the
catalogue twice and asserts one container per recipe (runtime/tests.rs 62–96).
These test bodies were inspected, not executed. Duplicate iterator counting is
therefore not an observed defect in the current loading caller.

The residency test waits for is_ready and checks loaded image bytes, sizes,
mips, formats and samplers against committed bakes (runtime/tests.rs 99–146).
It does not exercise installed_count, asset removal after installation or GPU
acknowledgement. The test was inspected but not run.

A repository-scoped exact call search found one installed_count caller, the
loading screen, and the specific resource initialization/reset patterns
searched found only plugin initialization. Generic resource operations and
native lifecycle behavior are not excluded by these searches. No additional
lens credit or runtime claim is assigned.

The prior residency body already owned the requested map, installed set and
installation flow. The current delta adds a count over that existing set and
does not change installation or reset logic. Thus asset-lifetime questions are
inherited connected obligations, while the count's iterator semantics and
loading consumer are the new delta scope. No cross-lens credit is assigned.

StageProgress requires total > 0 and completed >= total, and clamps only the
displayed fraction (progress.rs 83–91). The current catalogue is nonempty and
static, so an empty total is not reachable through this observed caller. The
count's semantic unit is iterator entries, and the same catalogue supplies
both numerator population and denominator. No separate count type or change
is justified solely by this scoped caller evidence.

Queue entry 49 already owns per-recipe terminal failure versus pending state.
Entry 2934 separately owns recipe/channel admission before installation. The
new count reads the installed set and does not resolve either obligation. These
are explicit connected references, not an alias or closure decision.

The loading screen reads UntypedAssetLoadFailedEvent and reports the path for
required scene assets (loading_screen.rs 145–154). The required-asset filter
includes textures/procedural. This is a separate event path from residency's
installed count and preserves a path in the displayed failure, while the
observed branch does not carry the underlying error. Event timing and all
failure writers remain open under entry 49 and the existing loading contract.

The asset event reader runs in Update before advance_load in a chained system.
LoadingScreen::fail changes state only while Loading (loading_screen.rs 63–88).
An event read while Idle or after failure is consumed without changing the
phase. Whether real asset requests can fail before the load begins or during
retry requires scheduling and message-lifetime evidence. No such incident was
reproduced.

Presentation startup eagerly requests catalogue textures unless the lazy
resource is present (procedural_texture_setup.rs 11–28, presentation/mod.rs
247–256). Loading begins on a client observer, so requests may precede an
active loading phase. A failure arriving then could be consumed while Idle,
but actual asynchronous ordering and retry behavior need a supported witness.

Retry despawns existing clients and spawns a cloned connection. The client-add
observer starts a new LoadingRun (view.rs 186–209, loading_screen.rs 119–126).
This action does not itself reset residency or request textures again. Native
AssetServer behavior and other systems remain necessary to determine whether a
failed asset is retried or reported on a subsequent attempt.

Exact-symbol search in loading-screen source finds the asset failure reader
and retry action but no test references to those symbols. This limited search
does not exclude integration tests elsewhere or tests using indirect behavior.
A bounded witness should cover failure before Loading and a subsequent retry,
plus retained native asset status, before choosing a repair.

Cargo.lock pins bevy_asset 0.19.1 with checksum
1624eddbf2293441b2158506aba75e523432b898d9da26eb6ed3e20af4c7fd38.
Local source locators include AssetServer::reload and get_load_state. The
registry source has not yet been authenticated against the locked crate or
read as evidence. Register and verify the archive before relying on behavior.

Authenticated bevy_asset 0.19.1 source sets LoadState::Failed with an owned
error when processing a failure (server/info.rs 637–655), and get_load_state
returns the retained root state (server/mod.rs 1238–1249). A request can start
a failed load again when it reaches the asset server (info.rs 224–240).
Project residency request uses HashMap::entry(...).or_insert_with(server.load),
so a repeated request for an already-retained key does not call server.load.
The loading retry action does not itself request or reset residency. This is a
source-based lifecycle finding, not a reproduced failure or a complete native
asset lifecycle proof. Native read chunk 872d2d matched the locked archive.

The existing loading-readiness registration covers both runtime.rs revisions,
but its cited observations cover other rows. The recent current full-body read
(chunk 82afb8) and prior body read (52360b, lines 25–100) occurred after that
registration. Their lens-specific assessment and adoption are still required;
registration alone grants no credit. The current source object hashes remain
those in registration rows 0 and 1.

Runtime handles reserve stable destination images for explicit recipe/channel
pairs, with a separate transient blood mask (runtime/handles.rs 8–112).
Installation looks up each supplied pair and expects a destination. The
existing channel-admission entry 2934 owns that boundary. This exploratory
read does not close a path or transfer another lens's evidence.

BakedRecipe::from_bytes checks nonempty maps, finite metadata, dimensions,
mips, duplicate channels, payload length and trailing data (wire.rs 60–123).
The observed function does not validate that each channel belongs to the
identified recipe. This corroborates the scoped question already recorded in
entry 2934. Full admission policy and exact same-lens evidence remain open.

TextureRecipeDescriptor associates an ID with broad TextureOutput categories
(catalogue.rs 76–102). These categories differ in granularity from concrete
MapChannel values used by reserved handles, such as front/back leaf maps.
Therefore the catalogue is relevant existing ownership, but direct equivalence
or complete channel admission cannot be assumed without mapping those types.

The generator explicitly maps leaf recipes to seven concrete channels,
including separate front/back albedo and normal maps, and special recipes to
specific channel sets (bake.rs 145–225). This confirms that catalogue output
categories are broader than concrete map channels. Surface mapping and sparse
admission policy still need exact qualification before choosing an owner.

surface_maps emits Albedo, Normal, Height and Arm (bake.rs 136–143), matching
the four channels reserved by SurfaceTextureSet::load. Leaf and special
mappings likewise correspond to their observed reservations. This checks
fresh generator/reservation correspondence at source level, not malformed
bake admission, sparse-map policy, or runtime execution.

Compressed admission bounds decompression and rejects trailing compressed data
before delegating to from_bytes (bake/compressed.rs 19–35). RuntimeTextureLoader
then checks the recipe slug against the filename and converts maps to images,
without a recipe/channel membership check in its observed body. This connects
the existing admission question to the installer and count without asserting
that a malformed committed bake exists.

The parser accepts a nonempty unique subset without checking expected recipe
channels. The installer iterates only supplied maps and marks the recipe
installed afterward (runtime.rs 89–105). A missing expected map could therefore
leave its reserved default image while the recipe is counted installed, if
such a bake is admitted. Sparse-map policy and an actual witness remain open.

Entry 2934 already requires that accepted maps have destinations and required
consumers never see a missing required map under completed readiness. It keeps
exact required set versus documented allowed subset as an explicit policy
question. The newly traced installed_count is an additional downstream
consumer, not a new independent admission finding or resolved policy.

Entry 49 already requires recipe identity and original cause, distinguishes
pending from failure, preserves stable handles and calls for explicit retry
policy. The recent authenticated native evidence narrows its first remaining
item, but is_ready consumers, scheduling, impostor failure and full current
scope remain open. The draft must preserve those obligations verbatim in any
adoption and cannot mark the entry closed.

Current tactical-client locators for residency include art-demo readiness,
strategic-scene status and world setup, plus loading progress and presentation
setup. The art-demo request uses a chained resource call that the earlier
literal residency.request search missed. Inspect those complete bodies before
claiming a full consumer or retry census.

Art-demo exhibit selection requests nonempty recipe sets when AssetServer is
present. textures_ready treats a missing residency resource as ready and
otherwise uses is_ready. scenery_ready returns pending on textures before it
checks the oak impostor's failed load state (art_demo/residency.rs 57–62,
146–165). This confirms the previously retained ordering concern at current
source scope. Plugin/resource guarantees and test-only modes remain separate.

Strategic-scene status requires catalogue is_ready as part of installation,
and retain_scene returns early while it is false (status.rs 105–145, world.rs
51–70). Both use a required residency resource. The separate SceneAssetFailure
resource in status must be traced before claiming a missing error path.

Strategic status captures required asset failure events in Last and retains a
path-based string. It excludes readiness while that value is present and
publishes it through status_error (status.rs 63–90, 145–150, 194–206). The
scoped exact-name search found no reset writer. Confirm resource lifecycle and
all indirect writes before deciding retry/reset policy or asserting persistence.

StrategicScenePlugin installs the status resource once at plugin build and
initializes RetainedScene separately (strategic_scene/mod.rs 63–70). The scoped
source search found no explicit SceneAssetFailure removal or reconstruction.
That supports a persistent failure concern for a retained app, subject to
indirect resource operations and actual lifecycle verification.

Queue entry 1414 explicitly retains the required-asset event's owned cause,
path and ID, all failure writers, reset and scene scope. The strategic status
trace belongs as scoped evidence there and does not warrant a duplicate entry
on the current evidence. Its broader native and status obligations remain open.

Production art-demo setup installs presentation with lazy procedural textures;
presentation materials installs BakedTexturesPlugin, which initializes the
residency resource (art_demo.rs 167–176, materials.rs 37, runtime.rs 18–23).
The missing-resource branch is therefore not enough by itself to establish a
production defect. Test setup and plugin failure/lifecycle remain separate.

A studio switching test creates a bare World without AssetServer or texture
residency and exercises weapon exhibits (art_demo/residency.rs 281–310). A
separate cache test installs BakedTexturesPlugin (313–326). These fixtures show
resource-free studio coverage exists, but do not alone prove why textures_ready
uses its absent-resource branch or cover scenery failure timing.

Exhibit::texture_recipes returns explicit Oak and City sets and an empty set
for other IDs (exhibits.rs 52–96). Residency::is_ready over an empty iterator
returns true. Preserve that legitimate empty selection when designing typed
failure/readiness outcomes; missing resource is a distinct question.

spawn_pending removes pending scenery and stores an owned preparation error
in CurrentExhibit when scenery_ready returns Err. A false texture readiness
returns before the oak impostor check, so an already failed impostor remains
unreported through this path until texture readiness changes. The code path is
established; simultaneous failures have not been executed.

Art-demo report_readiness converts CurrentExhibit preparation errors into an
Unavailable status string, while pending scenery reports Loading. It also
checks root and recursive dependency failure for a studio scene handle
(art_demo.rs 244–307). Thus the blocked impostor check delays an existing
error-reporting path, rather than proving the consumer cannot display errors.

Selecting a different exhibit removes PendingScenery before requesting the new
one. Selecting the same current ID returns immediately (residency.rs 30–37).
This scopes cancellation and retry semantics: a repeated same-ID selection does
not itself reissue a request. UI controls and native retry behavior remain to
be traced before concluding the full user-facing recovery path.

The demo command drain sets a loading status and calls show for Show commands
(art_demo.rs 214–225). The scoped source search found no explicit texture retry
command; renderer failure text advises reload. Prefetch and host controls still
need inspection before treating that search as a complete recovery census.

Art-demo prefetch returns for scenery and loads only a non-current studio
exhibit (residency.rs 230–253). It does not issue the procedural texture
request in that body. Host commands and asset-server behavior remain separate.

The typed DemoCommand interface contains Show, Prefetch, Orbit, Zoom and Pan,
with no explicit texture retry command (art_demo.rs 38–57). Queue accepts those
commands and Show clears queued commands. A host can still reload or recreate
the app outside this interface, so this does not prove the complete host
recovery behavior.

The art-demo host uses viewer.mjs to send Show and Prefetch commands. A scoped
search locates reload advice for renderer errors but no texture-specific retry
control. This is a locator search, not complete host-body coverage. Register and
read the relevant host flow before making a final recovery claim.

Host selection sends Show and startup boots a runtime; pageshow restores status
polling for a cached page (viewer.mjs 110–149, 248–290). This partial body read
is registered but is not a full host-flow assessment. No texture retry action
is established by these ranges.

The host polls runtime status, displays Unavailable messages, and otherwise
shows Loading or hides the overlay when Ready (viewer.mjs 293–325). It can
select another exhibit, but these observed paths do not explicitly reload a
failed texture. This qualifies the status consumer without asserting a live
failure or closing the full host scope.

The host entry module calls mount once, and the inspected page body exposes
selection controls and a status overlay with no explicit retry button
(demo.js, index.html). Browser reload or external host behavior remains outside
this source observation. No runtime failure was reproduced.

RuntimeTextureLoader returns io::Error, propagates read and decompression
errors, and reports a filename/recipe mismatch before publishing maps
(runtime.rs 112–142). Bevy retains that loader error in LoadState::Failed;
project loading status currently displays path only. Exact error conversion
and presentation policy remain connected work, with no new alias inferred.

Authenticated Bevy AssetLoadError includes AssetLoaderError, which owns path,
loader name and an Arc<BevyError> and exposes path() and error() (server/mod.rs
2352–2440, read chunk 7c17d9). This supports preserving the native error as a
source rather than reducing it to a string. Exact integration and typed
project outcome remain to be designed after the audit gate.

Both tactical loading and strategic status use is_required_scene_asset, which
matches the procedural texture path prefix and two unarmed asset suffixes
(scene_readiness.rs 51–56). This is path-class filtering, not a per-request
identity or scene ownership check in the observed function. Existing entry
1414 retains event scope and reset questions.

An exact-symbol search finds the filter definition and its two production
callers, with no direct test references in tactical-client source. This does
not exclude indirect or external integration tests. Event ownership and stale
failure cases remain explicit acceptance questions.

Entry 1414 already has a city readiness view, while its asset-event/reset
question remains explicitly open. The texture event trace should append a
separate scoped view and preserve the city view and all other native/status
contracts. It must not treat a shared status consumer as proof of an alias.

Within the complete status.rs body, the only assignment to SceneAssetFailure
is Some(path message) in capture_asset_failures. update_status resets settled
frames on view change but does not clear that failure. This confirms the local
writer behavior, while app resource recreation and indirect operations remain
outside the source scope.

BrowserRuntimePlugin installs StrategicScenePlugin at app build regardless of
initial browser mode (browser_runtime.rs 124–146). This supports a retained
resource across mode changes within that app, but the actual host lifetime and
resource reset pathways still require qualification. No runtime persistence
incident is asserted.

Browser commands switch the BrowserMode resource within the existing world and
spawn/despawn client entities (browser_runtime.rs 207–235, 275–293). Those
observed branches do not recreate the app or reset SceneAssetFailure. The
complete command body and host lifecycle remain separate evidence scopes.

The complete browser command body queues release_scene on entering tactical.
release_scene replaces RetainedScene and clears scene entities, but its body
does not clear SceneAssetFailure (strategic_scene/mod.rs 287–296). This
supports persistence across that transition within the same app. Other queued
operations and host recreation still require qualification.

clear_scene_entities clears scene caches and entities, resets GPU state and
replaces ActiveVistaSurface, but its complete observed body does not remove or
reset SceneAssetFailure (presentation/demo_lifecycle.rs 20–74). Nested GPU
reset and broader host lifecycle remain separate. This is exploratory evidence.

The nested GPU reset clears owner-specific city readiness, buffers, pending
cities and anchors (buildings.rs 37–42, buildings/gpu/mod.rs 103–123). Its
observed body does not touch the strategic asset-failure resource. This narrows
the direct release path, without proving all app or host lifecycle paths.

The WASM export wasm_strategic_status returns the strategic status JSON
(main.rs 222–226). This locates the native-to-host boundary for the retained
path error. Host polling and interpretation need their own source scope before
claiming user-facing impact.

The strategic host polls wasm_strategic_status and sends any state.error to
fail before considering readiness (strategic-scene.js 323–338). This connects
the stored message to host failure handling. The fail body and reset/restart
behavior remain to be inspected before asserting the resulting UI lifecycle.

The strategic host failure handler displays a generic Scene unavailable status
and logs the passed error (strategic-scene.js 79–88). A scene error from the
status poll reaches this handler. This is source-level behavior; exact host
recovery, visibility conditions and runtime incidents remain unverified.

An exact-symbol search across crates finds two untyped asset-failure readers:
tactical loading and strategic status. Typed asset events, indirect wrappers,
other repositories and native emitters are not excluded. This narrows the
project reader census without establishing complete failure ownership.

The wider exact-symbol search also finds typed AnimationClip and Gltf failure
readers. They use failure IDs to invalidate animation revisions
(animation/clip_revision/events.rs). This is a distinct owner and must not be
merged with texture residency merely because both consume asset events.

The queue already references animation/clip_revision/events.rs in entries
812, 828, 829 and 3779. Preserve those as independent candidate ownership
links. Exact alias and failure-cause requirements must be checked before
relating them to asset-event status work.

The bounded queue comparison identifies entry 829 as a conditional animation
cache-invalidation question and entry 3779 as its broader revision and schedule
investigation. Entry 828 concerns measured contact and phase dependencies;
entry 812 is a general historical audit-status note. These shared source
references alone do not establish aliases with strategic scene asset failure or
texture residency. No queue disposition or closure follows from this lookup.

At pinned revision ff9c1d7, runtime/tests.rs's committed-collection test
finds each baked map by searching all Image assets for matching pixel bytes,
then compares metadata and totals the maps. It collects the intended handles
but uses their count, not those handle identities, in that loop. Thus this
source test does not independently establish every map was placed into its
specific intended handle, despite its comment. It tests committed bakes, not
invalid channel admission. No test was executed. The complete source was read
in tool chunk 02cb5a; handle reservation was read in 0991c1, and the full
runtime path in the immediately preceding pinned git-show output. Keep this as
a scoped test-coverage limitation under the existing channel-admission
obligation, not a claim of an observed misbinding.

Correction: the earlier working-tree exact-symbol search in this continuation
was against the older checkout, not the selected revision. It is a locator only.
A pinned git grep independently confirms the narrow server/netcode and named
viewer paths, but is not a complete client insertion census.

Further pinned-source observations: `melee_defense.rs:60-105` compares typed
attack coordinates, derives a checked elapsed response delay and projects its
seconds only for the final timing ratio. `melee_round/commitment.rs:142-217`
admits defensive work and recovery durations as `AnimationElapsed` and retains
that type in every `DefenseCommitment` branch. Queue entries 669, 675, 686 and
729 also address P02 time ownership or scheduling under Lens 1; they overlap
in subject but carry additional open requirements, so this observation does not
establish that their contracts are identical or closed.

Native report and error path (selected revision): core `autoresolve/error.rs`
wraps elapsed and battle-time errors in `BattleResolutionError`; strategic
`combat_error.rs` transparently wraps that in `StrategicCombatError`.
`encounters.rs:1018-1055` propagates a resolution failure before committing
the outcome. `autoresolve.rs:181-234` formats a successful outcome into a

At `dcd6ea1aaddb0e542a418ae7ebe35c0bf73d4ecc`,
`animation/jitter.rs::analyze_scenario` computes local position velocity from
frames 0..n, then acceleration from that velocity using `frames[1..]`. The
resulting acceleration samples correspond to original frames 2..n. It then
computes position jerk using the unshifted frame slice and reports both

acceleration and jerk with `frames[2..]` and `frames[3..]`, respectively, while
preserving the rest of the derivative policy and verifying actual consumers.
